proposals.before: In the first year of Yongshi (33 BCE) he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Xindu at the Capital Township of Xinye in Nanyang, with fifteen hundred households.
proposals.after: In the first year of Yongshi (16 BCE) he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Xindu at the Capital Township of Xinye in Nanyang, with fifteen hundred households.
proposals.reason: Yongshi 1 of Han Chengdi corresponds to 16 BCE, not 33 BCE (the latter is the close of Emperor Yuan's reign).

proposals.before: Once he secretly purchased a maidservant. When his brothers got wind of it, Mang explained: "Rear General Zhu Boyuan has no son. I have heard that this girl's lineage is auspicious for bearing heirs, so I bought her for him."
proposals.after: Once he secretly purchased a maidservant. When his brothers got wind of it, Mang explained: "Rear General Zhu Ziyuan has no son. I have heard that this girl's lineage is auspicious for bearing heirs, so I bought her for him."
proposals.reason: The Chinese 硃子元 is Zhu Ziyuan; Boyuan would require 伯元, which is not present.

proposals.before: Dai Chong of Changle, Jin She, Ji Hong, Yang Bing, and Chen Tang—all famed men of the day—spoke for him, and the emperor came to esteem Mang.
proposals.after: Dai Chong, Lesser Treasury of Changle, together with Jin She, Ji Hong, Yang Bing, and Chen Tang—all famed men of the day—spoke for him, and the emperor came to esteem Mang.
proposals.reason: 長樂少府 is Dai Chong's office, not a native-place phrase 'of Changle'.

proposals.before: Recalled to Chang'an, Mang tried to visit Xiu; Xiu feigned sickness and shut his door.
proposals.after: When Mang was summoned away, he tried to visit Xiu; Xiu feigned sickness and shut his door.
proposals.reason: Chinese 徵去 does not name Chang'an; the place is an invented gloss.

proposals.before: A year after his recall Ai died heirless; Fu and Ding were already in their tombs. The grand empress dowager raced to Weiyang that day, seized the seals of office, and sent a flying summons for Mang.
proposals.after: More than a year after Mang returned to the capital, Emperor Ai died without an heir; Grand Empress Dowager Fu and Empress Dowager Ding had both already died. The grand empress dowager that same day drove to Weiyang Palace, seized the seals and ribbons, and sent a courier galloping to summon Mang.
proposals.reason: 歲餘 is more than a year, not a round year; 傅太后 and 丁太后 are titled dowagers, not bare surnames.

proposals.before: First a wind in Yizhou prompted a report that outer barbarians beyond the passes had presented white pheasants,
proposals.after: At first he hinted that Yizhou should have the outer barbarians beyond the passes present white pheasants,
proposals.reason: 風 here is to hint or instruct, not a meteorological wind.

proposals.before: At first a cyclone prompted the Yi prefecture to report that outer barbarians beyond the passes presented white pheasants,
proposals.after: At first he hinted that Yizhou should order the outer barbarians beyond the passes to present white pheasants,
proposals.reason: 風 is not a cyclone; 益州 is the command/prefecture instructed.

proposals.before: He wore severity and righteous speech; a hint from him brought a orchestrated memorial from his clique; he then wept and declined—duping the dowager above and the crowd below.
proposals.after: He wore severity and righteous speech; a hint from him brought an orchestrated memorial from his clique; he then wept and declined—duping the dowager above and the crowd below.
proposals.reason: English article error: 'a orchestrated' should be 'an orchestrated'.

proposals.before: The Masters' director Xun was told to command him: "You feign illness over the nomination; your post cannot stand empty—come now."
proposals.after: The Director of the Imperial Secretariat Xun was told to command him: "You feign illness over the nomination; your post cannot stand empty—come now."
proposals.reason: 尚書令 is the Director of the Imperial Secretariat, not a 'Masters' director'.

proposals.before: The empress dowager ordered Director of the Masters of Reading Xun to summon him with an edict: "You decline on the excuse of selection; your burden is heavy and may not be vacant; rise at once for the appointed time."
proposals.after: The empress dowager ordered Director of the Imperial Secretariat Xun to summon him with an edict: "You decline on the excuse of selection; your burden is heavy and may not be vacant; rise at once for the appointed time."
proposals.reason: 尚書令 is not the Masters of Reading; that English office name misrenders the Shangshu directorate.

proposals.before: Wang Shun of Anyang, general of chariots and cavalry, welcomed the prince with merit beyond the passes—add ten thousand households and make him grand guardian.
proposals.after: Wang Shun of Anyang, general of chariots and cavalry, welcomed the prince of Zhongshan and dashed enemies a myriad li away—add ten thousand households and make him grand guardian.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic line drops 中山王 and compresses 折衝萬里 into a vague 'beyond the passes', reversing the military sense.

proposals.before: Mang received the titles grand tutor and Duke Who Pacifies Han, declined returning the added fief, adjusted noble rank, and fief matters, saying he wished to wait until the hundred surnames each had enough at home, then receive added reward.
proposals.after: Mang received the titles grand tutor and Duke Who Pacifies Han, declined and returned the added fief and the adjustment of noble rank and fief, saying he wished to wait until the hundred surnames each had enough at home, then receive added reward.
proposals.reason: 讓還 means he declined and gave back the extra grant; 'declined returning' reverses the action.

proposals.before: He also sent Wang Zhaojun's daughter, the Xubu junior chief, to enter and attend.
proposals.after: He also sent Wang Zhaojun's daughter, the Xubu Juci, to enter and attend.
proposals.reason: 須卜居次 is a Xiongnu title for a princess married into the Xubu, not 'junior chief' as her own office.

proposals.before: Mang feared they would compete with his own daughter and immediately reported: "Your servant lacks virtue; his son's talents are low. It is not fitting that she be gathered together with the host of girls."
proposals.after: Mang feared they would compete with his own daughter and immediately reported: "Your servant lacks virtue; his child's talents are low. It is not fitting that she be gathered together with the host of girls."
proposals.reason: Chinese 子材下 in this memorial concerns Mang's daughter being listed among the girls, not a son.

proposals.before: Mang asked: "I beg to see the girl."
proposals.after: The dukes and ministers contended: "It is not fitting to gather the other girls and thereby split the legitimate line."
proposals.reason: Chinese 公卿爭曰不宜采諸女以貳正統 is the ministers' objection, not Mang asking to see the girl (that is s0152).

proposals.before: Mang reported: "We beg to see the girl."
proposals.after: The dukes and ministers contended: It is not fitting to gather the various girls and thereby make a second orthodox line.
proposals.reason: Literal English copies s0152 and invents Mang as speaker against 公卿爭曰.

proposals.before: Ministers said: "The queen's bride-gifts barely exceed the concubines' by a little."
proposals.after: Ministers said: "The empress's bride-gifts barely exceed the concubines' by a little."
proposals.reason: 皇后 is the empress, not a queen.

proposals.before: It opened with Mang's youth amid Wang luxury, yet choosing thrift and ritual against the tide;
proposals.after: It opened with the Duke Who Pacifies Han from his first coming of age amid an age of extravagance, favored by the two palaces and his uncles, yet choosing thrift and ritual against the tide;
proposals.reason: 兩宮 is the two palaces, not 'Wang luxury'; 束脩 and the uncles' glory are omitted or recast.

proposals.before: Emperor Ai saw Dong Hong invent dual lineages—Mang impeached him and set the record straight.
proposals.after: When Emperor Ai acceded, Marquis of Gaochang Dong Hong, currying favor, invented dual legitimacies; the Duke personally impeached him and thereby fixed the great ordinances.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic 'saw' omits 即位 and compresses 高昌侯 and 公手劾; the Chinese dates the impeachment to Ai's accession.

proposals.before: He barred Lady Fu from the imperial dais to preserve protocol.
proposals.after: He submitted that the Grand Empress Dowager of Dingtao ought not occupy the imperial curtained seat, thereby making the state's form clear.
proposals.reason: Lady Fu under-ranks 定陶太后 and drops the memorial (建白) and 乘輿幄坐 protocol.

proposals.before: Grand Empress Dowager of Dingtao wished to establish a presumptuous title; she dreaded the face-to-face rebuke of the curtained-seat righteousness; the bravado of flatterers, the likes of Zhu Bo, punished by the long and Hong impeachments—above and below one heart, slanderous villains crossed in confusion, crooked systems followed, until usurping titles were achieved, benevolent worthies were driven off, affinal kin were slaughtered, while the Duke suffered the complaint of Xu and Yuan, went far to his state, court government collapsed, cords and statutes were cast aside, and the peril of ruin hung no thicker than a hair.
proposals.after: Grand Empress Dowager of Dingtao wished to establish a presumptuous title; she dreaded the face-to-face rebuke of the curtained-seat righteousness; the bravado of flatterers, the likes of Zhu Bo, chastened by the impeachments of Chang and Hong—above and below one heart, slanderous villains crossed in confusion, crooked systems followed, until usurping titles were achieved, benevolent worthies were driven off, affinal kin were slaughtered, while the Duke suffered the complaint of Xu and Yuan, went far to his state, court government collapsed, cords and statutes were cast aside, and the peril of ruin hung no thicker than a hair.
proposals.reason: 長 is the name Chang (with 宏 Hong), not the adjective 'long'.

proposals.before: It paints a nightmare: Dong Xian and Fu kin forging wills and purging Zhongshan—had Mang not returned, coup was certain.
proposals.after: At that time offices lacked a stored heir; Dong Xian held heavy power, and the Fu further had a daughter's support. All knew themselves guilty toward the realm and bound in enmity to Zhongshan; they would surely share one worry, join as if breaking metal, borrow forged testamentary edicts, apply rewards and executions in turn, first removing those they feared and urgently drawing in those they leaned on, then falsely charging old wrongs and further punishing distant kin—once the situation lay open, nothing would have been difficult.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic sentence invents a narrator's 'nightmare' and 'coup' summary and drops 官亡儲主, the Fu daughter, and the forged-edict sequence.

proposals.before: The 《Documents》 says, 'Shun yielded to one whose virtue did not succeed him'—this speaks of the Duke.
proposals.after: The Documents says, 'Shun yielded on account of virtue and did not [force] the succession'—this speaks of the Duke.
proposals.reason: 舜讓於德不嗣 is Shun yielding from virtue rather than succeeding by force, not yielding to a person whose virtue did not succeed him.

proposals.before: Like Yu's dark jade and the Duke of Zhou's sacrifice to heaven, he claims no credit that belongs to the skies.
proposals.after: Therefore Bo Yu received the black jade tablet and the Duke of Zhou received suburban sacrifice, for they were heaven's envoys and did not dare monopolize heaven's merit.
proposals.reason: 伯禹 is Yu (Bo Yu), not 'Gun Yu'; 郊祀 is suburban sacrifice, and 不敢擅天之功 is the point of the comparison.

proposals.before: Gaozu never tired of rewarding a single good word—even a lowly guard who spoke for Fan Kuai won two thousand households.
proposals.after: Gaozu never tired of rewarding a single good word—therefore Gongsun Rong, though only an attendant drawn from the plume-headed guard, for one clear word about Fan Kuai received two thousand households.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic English drops the named individual 公孫戎 and fuses him into an unnamed 'lowly guard', erasing a person the Chinese identifies.

proposals.before: Xuandi fattened Huo Guang's fief and spread titles through his nephews.
proposals.after: Xuandi increased Huo Guang's households and spread titles through his elder brothers' grandsons.
proposals.reason: 兄孫 is grandsons of elder brothers, not nephews; 'fattened' also distorts 增戶命疇.

proposals.before: Zhou Bo leaned on kinship armies and a sordid coup—hardly a clean precedent.
proposals.after: Zhou Bo relied on the solidity of Han's feudatories, the stubbornness of Zhuxu, the relays of the generals, and mutual support—though the affair was ugly, in the end it could not succeed.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic version erases the named 朱虛 and invents 'kinship armies' and a completed 'coup' that the Chinese says could not succeed.

proposals.before: Mang memorialized: "Yu was misled by Lu Kuan and others, spread rumors and confused the multitude, and shares guilt with Guan and Cai. Your servant dared not conceal this, and begs execution."
proposals.after: Mang memorialized: "Yu was misled by Lü Kuan and others, spread rumors and confused the multitude, and shares guilt with Guan and Cai. Your servant dared not conceal this, and begs execution."
proposals.reason: Lu Kuan misspells 呂寬, elsewhere Lü Kuan in the same translation.

proposals.before: Mang used the case to wipe out the Wei, implicate every critic, and drive Princess Jingwu, two princes Li, and Wang Ren to suicide.
proposals.after: Mang used the case to wipe out the Wei, exhaustively try Lü Kuan's case, and drive Princess Jingwu, Liang prince Li, the marquis of Hongyang Li, and the marquis of Ping'e Ren to suicide.
proposals.reason: 梁王立 and 紅陽侯立 are a prince and a marquis, both named Li, not 'two princes Li'; 平阿侯仁 is a marquis, not grouped as Wang Ren alone against two princes.

proposals.before: And more than eight thousand commoners who submitted memorials all said: yiyin day was made Ah Heng, the Duke of Zhou was made grand steward; the Duke of Zhou enjoyed enfeoffments for seven sons, receiving reward surpassing the supreme duke.
proposals.after: And more than eight thousand commoners who submitted memorials all said: Yi Yin was made Aheng, the Duke of Zhou was made grand steward; the Duke of Zhou enjoyed enfeoffments for seven sons, receiving reward surpassing the supreme duke.
proposals.reason: The literal line corrupts 伊尹 as “yiyin day” instead of the personal name Yi Yin.

proposals.before: The memorial was handed to the responsible officials; they requested returning the two counties earlier added plus Huangyou cluster and Xinye fields, adopting yiyin day and the Duke of Zhou's titles, adding to the Duke the title Regulator-and-Balance, rank above the supreme duke.
proposals.after: The memorial was handed to the responsible officials; they requested returning the two counties earlier added plus Huangyou cluster and Xinye fields, adopting Yi Yin’s and the Duke of Zhou’s titles, adding to the Duke the title Regulator-and-Balance, rank above the supreme duke.
proposals.reason: The literal line again corrupts 伊尹 as “yiyin day” rather than Yi Yin’s titles.

proposals.before: When the Three Dukes speak on affairs they shall say 'We presume to speak.
proposals.after: When the Three Dukes speak on affairs they shall say 'We presume to speak.'
proposals.reason: The quoted deferential formula is left unclosed.

proposals.before: Let Mang return the extra land he promised for moral example.
proposals.after: The fields at Huangyou, Zhaoling, and Xinye that were yielded in are especially many and all remain with the Duke; the Duke wishes to reduce himself to complete the state’s transformation—it is fitting to grant permission.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic line omits the named fields and misstates the officials’ request, which is to allow Mang’s self-reduction.

proposals.before: Thirty-six imperial descendants named Xin became marquises; others got bumps in rank or gold.
proposals.after: When the rites finished, Xin and thirty-five other great-great-grandsons of Emperor Xiaoxuan, thirty-six men, were enfeoffed as full marquises; the rest all had households increased or noble rank granted, with gold and silk rewards each according to number.
proposals.reason: Chinese 孝宣曾孫信第三十六人 names Xin as the lead among thirty-six great-great-grandsons of Emperor Xiaoxuan, not thirty-six men who all bore the personal name Xin.

proposals.before: When the rites finished, thirty-six of Xiaoxuan's great-great-grandsons bearing the name Xin were enfeoffed as full marquises; the rest all had households increased or noble rank granted, gold and silk rewards each according to number.
proposals.after: When the rites finished, Xin and thirty-five others among Xiaoxuan's great-great-grandsons, thirty-six men, were enfeoffed as full marquises; the rest all had households increased or noble rank granted, gold and silk rewards each according to number.
proposals.reason: 信第三十六人 is a count of thirty-six descendants headed by Xin, not a statement that each bore the name Xin.

proposals.before: no ministers surpassed yiyin day and the Duke of Zhou—yet Mang is paired with them.
proposals.after: no ministers surpassed Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou—yet Mang is paired with them.
proposals.reason: 伊 is the minister Yi Yin; the English fused it into the nonsense phrase yiyin day.

proposals.before: That fall Mang cut the Ziwu road through the mountains, citing the queen's pregnancy omen.
proposals.after: That autumn, because the empress had an auspice of offspring, Mang opened the Ziwu road.
proposals.reason: 皇后 is the empress, not a queen; 子孫瑞 is an omen of offspring, and 通子午道 is opening the Ziwu road.

proposals.before: The forged Qiang reply listed every miracle—giant grain, self-grown crops, phoenixes, sweet dew—
proposals.after: When asked why Liangyuan submitted, they answered that the grand empress dowager was sage-bright and the Duke Who Pacifies Han supremely benevolent, listing bumper harvests, unsown crops, sweet dew, phoenixes, and divine sparrows.
proposals.reason: The Chinese is a reported Qiang reply praising the dowager and Mang; the idiomatic English invents 'forged' and drops the named speakers.

proposals.before: Mang copied King Wu's metal coffer rite, offering his life for the boy's at Tai.
proposals.after: When Emperor Ping fell ill, Mang composed a casket document, begged for Ping's life at the Grand Suburban Altar, wore the jade disk and held the tablet, and wished to substitute his own body.
proposals.reason: This sentence does not mention King Wu or a metal coffer; the coffer appears in the next unit.

proposals.before: He imposed three years' mourning on every official above six hundred bushels.
proposals.after: Mang summoned ritual experts such as Director of the imperial clan Feng and with them ordered that officials of six hundred bushels and above observe three years' mourning.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic line omits the named ritualist 宗伯鳳.

proposals.before: He picked the two-year-old Ying of Guangqi on forged omens.
proposals.after: He therefore chose the youngest of the great-great-grandsons, Ying, son of the Marquis of Guangqi, aged two, claiming that divination and physiognomy showed him most auspicious.
proposals.reason: The source claims auspicious divination; it does not say the omens were forged.

proposals.before: In the first month of the first year of acting regency, Mang sacrificed to High God at the southern suburb, welcomed spring at the eastern suburb, performed the great archery rite at the Bright Hall, nourished the three elders and five more-with-completed rites he departed.
proposals.after: In the first month of the first year of acting regency, Mang sacrificed to High God at the southern suburb, welcomed spring at the eastern suburb, performed the great archery rite at the Bright Hall, and nourished the Three Elders and Five Experienced Men; when the rites were complete he departed.
proposals.reason: The literal English fuses 五更 with 成禮而去.

proposals.before: Critics cowered—shame on the Liu.
proposals.after: Those under heaven who condemned him none dared be first to rise; this is the imperial house's shame.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic English omits 天下非之者乃莫敢先舉 and reduces 宗室恥 to a slogan.

proposals.before: A hundred men struck Wan and failed.
proposals.after: Shao and his followers, more than a hundred, advanced to attack Wan, could not enter, and were defeated.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic English drops Zhang Shao (紹等) as subject.

proposals.before: Between Jianping and Yuanshou Han nearly fell,
proposals.after: Between Jianping and Yuanshou the great succession nearly snapped,
proposals.reason: Yuanshou Han fuses era 元壽 with the dynasty; 大統幾絕 is the succession.

proposals.before: fighting beats flattery, but memorials beat fighting."
proposals.after: to fight hard is not as good as cleverly drafting a memorial."
proposals.reason: Chinese 力戰鬥，不如巧為奏 makes fighting inferior to a clever memorial; the idiomatic line reverses that.

proposals.before: She ennobled Wang Shun's sons Kuang and Lin, Kong Guang's grandson Shou, and Zhen Feng's grandson Kuang.
proposals.after: She enfeoffed Shun's son Kuang as Marquis of Shared Heart, Lin as Marquis of Pleasing Virtue, Guang's grandson Shou as Marquis of Joined Intent, and Feng's grandson Kuang as Marquis of Combined Strength.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic English drops the four marquis titles.

proposals.before: Wang Yi returned, crushed Zhao Ming and Huo Hong—see Zhai Yi's biography.
proposals.after: Wang Yi and the others returned to the capital and, joining Wang Ji and the others westward, crushed Zhao Ming and Huo Hong—the account is in the Biography of Zhai Yi.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic English drops 還京師 and the junction with 王級, collapsing a joint campaign into Wang Yi acting alone.

proposals.before: The 《Royal Regulations》 of the Record of Rites has more than seventeen hundred states; therefore Confucius wrote in the 《Classic of Filial Piety》: 'I dare not slight the ministers of small states—how much less dukes, marquises, earls, counts, and barons!
proposals.after: The 《Royal Regulations》 of the Record of Rites has more than seventeen hundred states; therefore Confucius wrote in the 《Classic of Filial Piety》: 'I dare not slight the ministers of small states—how much less dukes, marquises, earls, viscounts, and barons!
proposals.reason: 子 is viscount, not count; the literal line invents a second count rank already covered by 伯.

proposals.before: They cited yiyin day and Taijia,
proposals.after: They cited Yi Yin and Taijia:
proposals.reason: yiyin day is a garbled rendering of 伊尹, not a calendar day.

proposals.before: In old days when Yin Cheng Tang had passed away and the heir son died young, his son Taijia was young and not enlightened, yiyin day banished him to the Tong palace and dwelt as regent, thereby raising Yin's way.
proposals.after: In old days when Yin Cheng Tang had passed away and the heir son died young, his son Taijia was young and not enlightened; Yi Yin banished him to the Tong palace and dwelt as regent, thereby raising Yin's way.
proposals.reason: 伊尹 is the minister Yi Yin, not yiyin day.

proposals.before: The dowager made his grandson Zong marquis of Xindu to continue Man's line,
proposals.after: The dowager made his eldest grandson marquis of Xindu to continue Marquis Ai.
proposals.reason: 哀侯 is Marquis Ai; Man is an invented English name not in this unit.

proposals.before: The Documents' 'Kang Gao' 'The king spoke thus: "Marquises, my younger brother, young son Feng."
proposals.after: The Documents' 'Kang Gao': 'The king spoke thus: "Menghou, my younger brother, young son Feng."'
proposals.reason: 孟侯 is a singular title for Feng, not the English plural 'Marquises'.

proposals.before: “He donned the true king's crown, visited the empress dowager, returned to sit in Weiyang's forward hall, and issued a document: 'We, lacking virtue, rely on being after the august first ancestor the Yellow Emperor and the august first forebear Shun's line, and a distant twig of the grand empress dowager.
proposals.after: He donned the true king's crown, visited the empress dowager, returned to sit in Weiyang's forward hall, and issued a document: 'We, lacking virtue, rely on being after the august first ancestor the Yellow Emperor and the august first forebear Shun's line, and a distant twig of the grand empress dowager.
proposals.reason: The literal English is prefixed with a stray quotation mark that is not in the Chinese and fuses narration with the edict opening.

decisions.reason: 永始元年 falls in Chengdi’s Yongshi era (16 BCE). The original 33 BCE date belongs to the close of Yuandi’s reign, not this enfeoffment.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 永始元年，封莽為新都侯

decisions.reason: The personal name is 硃子元 (Zhu Ziyuan). Boyuan would require 伯元, which is not in the sentence.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 後將軍硃子元無子

decisions.after: Dai Chong, Lesser Treasurer of Changle, together with Jin She, Ji Hong, Yang Bing, and Chen Tang—all famed men of the day—spoke for him, and the emperor came to esteem Mang.
decisions.reason: 長樂少府 is Dai Chong’s office, not a native-place ‘of Changle’. The proposed apposition ‘Lesser Treasury of Changle’ names the bureau rather than the officer.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 長樂少府戴崇

decisions.reason: 及莽徵去 records a summons that took Mang away; the Chinese does not name Chang’an in this unit.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 及莽徵去，欲見休，休稱疾不見

decisions.reason: 歲餘 is more than a year, not a round year; 哀帝, 傅太后, and 丁太后 are titled persons, and 先薨 is prior death rather than a tomb scene.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 莽還京師歲餘，哀帝崩，無子，而傅太后、丁太后皆先薨

decisions.reason: 風益州令 is to hint or instruct Yizhou to have the barbarians present pheasants, not a meteorological wind prompting a report.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 始，風益州令塞外蠻夷獻白雉

decisions.reason: 風 is not a cyclone; 益州 is the jurisdiction ordered to have the outer barbarians present white pheasants.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 風益州令塞外蠻夷獻白雉

decisions.reason: The original English is ungrammatical: ‘a orchestrated’ must be ‘an orchestrated’.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 黨與承其指意而顯奏之

decisions.reason: 尚書令 is the Director of the Imperial Secretariat, not a ‘Masters’ director’.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 太后使尚書令恂詔之曰

decisions.reason: 尚書令 is not the Masters of Reading; that English office name misrenders the Shangshu directorate.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 太后使尚書令恂詔之曰

decisions.after: Marquis of Anyang Wang Shun, general of chariots and cavalry, welcomed the prince of Zhongshan and repelled enemies a myriad li away—add ten thousand households and make him grand guardian.
decisions.reason: The original drops 中山王 and flattens 折衝萬里. The proposal still treats 安陽侯 as a place-name ‘of Anyang’ and ‘dashed enemies’ is an awkward rendering of 折衝.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 車騎將軍安陽侯舜積累仁孝，使迎中山王，折衝萬里

decisions.reason: 讓還益封疇爵邑事 means he declined and gave back the added fief and the rank-and-fief adjustment; ‘declined returning’ reverses the action.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 莽受太傅安漢公號，讓還益封疇爵邑事

decisions.reason: 須卜居次 is the Xiongnu title Xubu Juci, not an office ‘junior chief’ held by the daughter herself.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 又遣王昭君女須卜居次入待

decisions.reason: In this memorial 子材下 refers to Mang’s child listed among the girls (與眾女並采), not a son.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 身亡德，子材下，不宜與眾女並采

decisions.reason: 公卿爭曰 introduces the ministers’ objection; the original copies Mang’s later request 願見女 from s0152.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 公卿爭曰：「不宜采諸女以貳正統。」

decisions.reason: The speakers are 公卿, not Mang, and the quoted objection is 不宜采諸女以貳正統, not a request to see the girl.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 公卿爭曰：「不宜采諸女以貳正統。」

decisions.reason: 皇后 is the Han empress; ‘queen’ under-ranks the title in this betrothal context.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 今皇后受聘，踰羣妾亡幾

decisions.reason: 兩宮 is the two palaces, not ‘Wang luxury’; the opening also names 安漢公, 束脩, and 諸父, which the original recasts or omits.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 竊見安漢公自初束脩，值世俗隆奢麗之時，蒙兩宮厚骨肉之寵，被諸父赫赫之光

decisions.reason: 孝哀即位 dates the episode to Ai’s accession; 高昌侯董宏 and 公手劾 are omitted or distorted by ‘saw’.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 孝哀即位，高昌侯董宏希指求美，造作二統，公手劾之，以定大綱

decisions.reason: The object is 定陶太后, not ‘Lady Fu’; 建白 and 乘輿幄坐 are a memorial about the imperial curtained seat.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 建白定陶太后不宜在乘輿幄坐，以明國體

decisions.reason: 長、宏 are the names Chang and Hong, not the adjective ‘long’ paired with Hong.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 懲此長、宏手劾之事

decisions.reason: The original invents a ‘nightmare’ and ‘coup’ summary and drops 官亡儲主, 傅氏有女之援, and the forged-edict sequence.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 當此之時，官亡儲主，董賢據重，加以傅氏有女之援

decisions.after: The 《Documents》 says, 'Shun yielded on account of virtue and did not succeed'—this speaks of the Duke.
decisions.reason: 舜讓於德不嗣 is Shun yielding on account of virtue and not taking the succession, not yielding to a person whose virtue failed. The proposal’s bracketed ‘[force]’ is an interpolation.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 《書》曰「舜讓於德不嗣，」公之謂矣

decisions.reason: 伯禹 is Bo Yu; he received the 玄圭, the Duke of Zhou received 郊祀, and the point is 不敢擅天之功.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 是以伯禹錫玄圭，周公受郊祀，蓋以達天之使，不敢擅天之功也

decisions.reason: The named attendant is 公孫戎; collapsing him into an unnamed ‘lowly guard’ erases the person the Chinese identifies.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 是故公孫戎位在充郎，選繇旄頭，一明樊噲，封二千戶

decisions.reason: 兄孫 is grandsons of elder brothers, not nephews; 增戶命疇 is increasing households and granting rank, not ‘fattening’ a fief.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 孝宣皇帝顯著霍光，增戶命疇，封者三人，延及兄孫

decisions.reason: The original erases 朱虛, invents ‘kinship armies’ and a completed coup, and ignores 其事雖醜，要不能遂.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 夫絳侯即因漢藩之固，杖朱虛之鯁，依諸將之遞，據相扶之勢，其事雖醜，要不能遂

decisions.reason: 呂寬 is Lü Kuan; Lu Kuan misspells the surname 呂.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 宇為呂寬等所詿誤

decisions.after: Mang used the case to wipe out the Wei, exhaustively try Lü Kuan's case, implicate regional stalwarts who had long criticized him, and drive Princess Jingwu, Liang prince Li, the Marquis of Hongyang Li, and the Marquis of Ping'e Ren to suicide.
decisions.reason: 梁王立 and 紅陽侯立 are a prince and a marquis both named Li, and 平阿侯仁 is a marquis. The proposal still omits 連引郡國豪桀素非議已者.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 莽因是誅滅衛氏，窮治呂寬之獄，連引郡國豪桀素非議已者，內及敬武公主、梁王立、紅陽侯立、平阿侯仁

decisions.reason: 伊尹 is the minister Yi Yin, not a ‘yiyin day’.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 伊尹為阿衡，周公為太宰

decisions.reason: 采伊尹、周公稱號 means adopting Yi Yin’s and the Duke of Zhou’s titles, not a ‘yiyin day’.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 采伊尹、周公稱號

decisions.reason: The quoted formula 敢言之 is left unclosed in the original English.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 三公言事，稱『敢言之』

decisions.reason: The named fields are 黃郵、召陵、新野; the officials ask that the Duke’s wish to reduce himself be granted, not that extra land be forced back as a moral example.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 黃郵、召陵、新野之田為入尤多，皆止於公，公欲自損以成國化，宜可聽許

decisions.reason: 孝宣曾孫信第三十六人 names Xin as the first of thirty-six great-great-grandsons, not thirty-six men who all bore the name Xin.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 封孝宣曾孫信第三十六人為列侯

decisions.reason: 信第三十六人 is a count headed by Xin, not a statement that each of the thirty-six bore that name.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 封孝宣曾孫信第三十六人為列侯

decisions.reason: 伊、周 are Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou; ‘yiyin day’ is a garbled fusion, not a calendar day.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 忠臣茂功莫著於伊、周，而宰衡配之

decisions.reason: 皇后 is the empress; 子孫瑞 is an auspice of offspring, and 通子午道 is opening the Ziwu road, not cutting mountains on a ‘queen’s pregnancy omen’.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 其秋，莽以皇后有子孫瑞，通子午道

decisions.reason: This unit is Liangyuan’s reported reply praising the grand empress dowager and the Duke; the original invents ‘forged’ and drops the named speakers.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 問良願降意，對曰：『太皇太后聖明，安漢公至仁

decisions.after: When Emperor Ping fell ill, Mang composed a document, begged for Ping's life at the Grand Suburban Altar, wore the jade disk and held the tablet, and wished to substitute his own body.
decisions.reason: This unit has 作策 and 請命於泰畤, not King Wu or a metal coffer. The proposal’s ‘casket document’ borrows 金滕 from the next sentence.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 平帝疾，莽作策，請命於泰畤，戴璧秉圭，願以身代

decisions.reason: 莽徵明禮者宗伯鳳等 names the ritualist Feng; the original omits him and turns ‘six hundred bushels and above’ into ‘above six hundred’.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 莽徵明禮者宗伯鳳等與定天下吏六百石以上皆服喪三年

decisions.reason: 託以為卜相最吉 claims auspicious divination and physiognomy; the Chinese does not say the omens were forged.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 乃選玄孫中最幼廣戚侯子嬰，年二歲，託以為卜相最吉

decisions.reason: 三老五更 is the pair of honorifics Three Elders and Five Experienced Men; 成禮而去 is a separate clause, not ‘five more-with-completed rites’.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 養三老五更，成禮而去

decisions.after: None of those under heaven who condemned him dared be first to rise; this is the imperial house's shame.
decisions.reason: The original slogan omits 天下非之者乃莫敢先舉. The proposal restores the sense but is ungrammatical English.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 天下非之者，乃莫敢先舉，此宗室恥也

decisions.reason: 紹等從者百餘人 makes Zhang Shao and his followers the subject, not an unnamed hundred men.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 紹等從者百餘人，遂進攻宛，不得入而敗

decisions.reason: 元壽 is the era Yuanshou, not ‘Yuanshou Han’; 大統幾絕 is the great succession nearly snapping.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 建平、元壽之間，大統幾絕

decisions.reason: 力戰鬥，不如巧為奏 makes hard fighting inferior to a clever memorial; the original reverses that ranking.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 力戰鬥，不如巧為奏

decisions.reason: The edict grants four distinct marquisates—同心侯, 說德侯, 合意侯, 並力侯—which the original drops.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 封舜了匡為同心侯，林為說德侯，光孫壽為合意侯，豐孫匡為並力侯

decisions.reason: 王邑等還京師 and 西與王級等合擊 name a return to the capital and a junction with Wang Ji, not Wang Yi acting alone.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 王邑等還京師，西與王級等合擊明、鴻，皆破滅

decisions.after: The 《Royal Regulations》 of the Record of Rites has more than seventeen hundred states; therefore Confucius wrote in the 《Classic of Filial Piety》: 'I dare not slight the ministers of small states—how much less dukes, marquises, earls, viscounts, and barons!'
decisions.reason: 子 is viscount, not a second ‘count’ already covered by 伯. The proposal still leaves the quoted sentence unclosed.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 而況於公、侯、伯、子、男乎？

decisions.reason: 伊尹 is Yi Yin; ‘yiyin day’ is a garbled rendering of the minister’s name, not a calendar day.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 伊尹放諸桐宮而居攝

decisions.reason: 伊尹 is the minister who banished Taijia to the Tong palace and acted as regent, not ‘yiyin day’.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 其子太甲幼少不明，伊尹放諸桐宮而居攝，以興殷道

decisions.reason: The heir is 元孫 made 侯新都 to continue 哀侯; ‘Zong’ and ‘Man’ are not in this unit.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 故太皇太后建厥元孫，俾侯新都，為哀侯後

decisions.reason: 孟侯 is a singular address to Feng, not the English plural ‘Marquises’.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 王若曰：『孟侯，朕其弟，小子封。』
